'''András Vasy''' (born 1969) is a Hungarian–American mathematician working in the areas of [[partial differential equations]], [[microlocal analysis]], [[scattering theory]], and [[inverse problems]]. He is currently a professor of mathematics at [[Stanford University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=András Vasy's Stanford Homepage |url=http://virtualmath1.stanford.edu/~andras/ |access-date=2024-10-13 |website=virtualmath1.stanford.edu}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Vasy grew up in Budapest and attended Apáczai Csere János Gimnázium of the [[Eötvös Loránd University]] (ELTE). He then became a boarding-school student at the [[United World College of the Atlantic]] in Wales.<ref name=NoticesAMS/> Vasy attended [[Stanford University]], obtaining his BS in Physics and MS in mathematics in 1993. He received his PhD from [[MIT]] under the supervision of [[Richard Burt Melrose|Richard B. Melrose]] in 1997.<ref>[http://www.genealogy.ams.org/id.php?id=37030 András Vasy] in the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]</ref> Following his postdoctoral appointment at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], he joined the MIT faculty as an assistant professor in 1999. He was awarded tenure at MIT in 2005<ref>[https://news.mit.edu/2005/tenure-1019 "25 faculty members earn tenure"]</ref> during a long-term stay at Northwestern University before moving to Stanford in 2006.

== Awards and honors ==

Vasy was an [[Sloan Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellow]] from 2002 to 2004,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sloan.org/past-fellows |title=List of past Sloan Fellows |access-date=November 19, 2016 |archive-date=March 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180314000756/https://sloan.org/past-fellows |url-status=dead }}</ref> and a [[Clay Mathematics Institute|Clay Research Fellow]] from 2004 to 2006.<ref>[http://www.claymath.org/people/andr%C3%A1s-vasy András Vasy] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170111113036/http://www.claymath.org/people/andr%C3%A1s-vasy |date=January 11, 2017 }}, Clay Mathematics Institute</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the American Mathematical Society in 2012. He was an invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Seoul in 2014.<ref>[http://www.icm2014.org/en/program/scientific/section.html Scientific program, Seoul ICM 2014]; [http://virtualmath1.stanford.edu/~andras/microloc-icm.pdf slides from Vasy's 2014 ICM talk]</ref><ref>{{cite book|author=Vasy, A.|year=2014|chapter=Some recent advances in microlocal analysis|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians-Seoul|volume=3|pages=915–939|chapter-url=https://virtualmath1.stanford.edu/~andras/icm-14.pdf}}</ref> In 2017, he was awarded the [[Bôcher Prize]] of the American Mathematical Society.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=3215 "Andras Vasy to Receive 2017 AMS Bôcher Prize"]</ref><ref name=NoticesAMS/>

== Research ==

The unifying feature of Vasy's work is the application of tools from microlocal analysis to problems in hyperbolic partial differential or pseudo-differential equations. He analyzed the propagation of singularities for solutions of wave equations on manifolds with corners<ref>András Vasy, [https://www.jstor.org/stable/40345428 "Propagation of singularities for the wave equation on manifolds with corners"], Annals of Mathematics 168, 749–812 (2008)</ref> or more complicated boundary structures, partially in joint work with [[Richard Burt Melrose|Richard Melrose]] and [[Jared Wunsch]].<ref>Jared Wunsch, András Vasy, and Richard B. Melrose, [https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.dmj/1215032812 "Propagation of singularities for the wave equation on edge manifolds"], Duke Math. J. 144(1), pp.&nbsp;109–193 (2008)</ref> For his paper on a unified approach to scattering theory on asymptotically hyperbolic spaces and spacetimes arising in Einstein's theory of [[general relativity]] such as [[de Sitter]] space and [[Roy Kerr|Kerr]]-de Sitter spacetimes,<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00222-012-0446-8 | doi=10.1007/s00222-012-0446-8 | title=Microlocal analysis of asymptotically hyperbolic and Kerr-de Sitter spaces (With an appendix by Semyon Dyatlov) | date=2013 | last1=Vasy | first1=András | journal=Inventiones Mathematicae | volume=194 | issue=2 | pages=381–513 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> he was awarded the [[Bôcher Prize]] in 2017. This paper led to further advances, including the proof, by Vasy and [[Peter Hintz]], of the global nonlinear stability of the Kerr-de Sitter family of black hole spacetimes,<ref>Peter Hintz and András Vasy, [https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.acta/1560966510 "The global non-linear stability of the Kerr–de Sitter family of black holes"], Acta Mathematica 220(1), pp.&nbsp;1–206 (2018)</ref> and a new proof of [[Stephen Smale|Smale]]'s conjecture for Anosov flows by [[Semyon Dyatlov]] and [[Maciej Zworski]].<ref>Semyon Dyatlov and Maciej Zworski, [http://smf4.emath.fr/Publications/AnnalesENS/4_49/html/ens_ann-sc_49_543-577.php "Dynamical zeta functions for Anosov flows via microlocal analysis"], Annales scientifiques de l'ENS 49(3), pp.&nbsp;543–577 (2016)</ref> Vasy has also collaborated with [[Gunther Uhlmann]] on inverse problems for geodesic transforms.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00222-015-0631-7 | doi=10.1007/s00222-015-0631-7 | title=The inverse problem for the local geodesic ray transform | date=2016 | last1=Uhlmann | first1=Gunther | last2=Vasy | first2=András | journal=Inventiones Mathematicae | volume=205 | pages=83–120 | arxiv=1210.2084 }}</ref>
